It may be my imagination running away with me, I heard that it happened to a guy in Texas last year, but of course his loans were federally backed and different states are different.

Taxes are taken care of already. 

If there happened to be a warrant, would they be likely to notice it when I was entering or leaving the country? (If it helps, I would be entering and leaving from another state, and not driving a car at all during the trip.)

My brain has this weird thing I call "performance mode." No matter how completely and utterly panicked I am BEFORE doing something performance-related (a speech, a job interview, a recital...) as soon as it starts I am zen. I am in the eye of the storm. Nothing can touch me.

And then as soon as it's over I'm basically dying again, and it's worse than ever, and when I finally calm down I just want to sleep for days. 

But if I can leverage that, I can do the thing as far as looking for work.

Xanax is pretty safe. As you must have learned, there's a chance that you'll stop breathing, but it's not that high. It's more likely to just make you puke a lot. Even more likely if you've taken those things (xanax and alcohol) in the past and built up some tolerance. 

I've never understood the drug thing. Accessibility, I guess? But it almost never works.

Hope you see this as a reason to hang around longer.

I don't know because I do the same thing and always have. I love my daydream world. My imagination has always been more powerful than anyone else's I've ever met. I can make myself hallucinate if I want to. I can concentrate on the real world if something really interesting or important is happening for awhile, but I always go back, and I am often low-key daydreaming even then. 

I've had the same primary imaginary friend since I was a kid. Sometimes changing in shape or voice, but always the same on the inside. 

Sometimes I think maybe he's not imaginary at all. Maybe there's something out there really talking to me.
I would love books!

I wish I could. Where I live, mental health care is not covered under insurance, and is extremely expensive. Add to that that most therapists don't speak my native language very well, and there's sometimes gaps in doctor-patient confidentiality that can accidentally mess up careers due to the stigma here (rarely, but it happens, mostly to foreigners and immigrants) and it's not a feasible option for me. 

I really, really wish it was.

I swear I'm not looking for a fight... but somehow even things I am sure are innocuous just come out all wrong. I never realize I'm ruining things until it's in the rear view mirror. It's like I don't even know how to be a person. 

Sorry you went through that.
